facts.content: Patient has acute dizziness and vertigo.
Patient experienced sudden onset vertigo approximately 2 hours ago while making breakfast, with a constant sensation of the room spinning.
facts.source_text: Sudden onset vertigo ~2 hrs ago while making breakfast; constant; room spinning

facts.content: Patient has an unsteady gait and can walk but not straight.
facts.source_text: Unsteady gait; can walk but not straight

facts.content: Patient is experiencing ear buzzing but no hearing loss, ear pain, or ear discharge.
facts.source_text: Ear buzzing; no hearing loss; no otalgia/otorrhea

facts.content: Patient has nausea but no vomiting.
Patient denies recent upper respiratory infection or fever.
Patient experienced a similar brief episode about one month ago which lasted 5 to 10 minutes and resolved on its own.
facts.source_text: Similar brief episode ~1 mo ago (5–10 min), self-resolved

facts.content: Patient has a history of premature ovarian failure.
Patient is on hormone replacement therapy (HRT).
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Diagnosis of acute labyrinthitis with continuous vertigo for 2 hours, tinnitus, and gait unsteadiness.
facts.source_text: Acute labyrinthitis — continuous vertigo x2 hrs with tinnitus and gait unsteadiness; no focal weakness; no recent viral sx

facts.content: Nausea is associated with the vertigo.
Patient has chronic premature ovarian failure and is on hormone replacement therapy.
Prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy for labyrinthitis or vertigo, with instructions to take one tablet three times daily for 10 days.
facts.source_text: Rx sent to Lloyds Pharmacy — 1 tab TID x10 days (drug name not captured)

facts.content: Arrange an in-person appointment for ear examination, blood pressure check, and gait or neurologic assessment within the next few days.
facts.source_text: In-person review: Arrange appt in next few days for ear exam, BP, gait/neurologic assessment

facts.content: Safety-net by instructing patient to attend A&E if experiencing new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or persistent or violent vomiting.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Attend A&E if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or persistent/violent vomiting

facts.content: Medication can be taken without food if needed.
facts.source_text: Med admin: May take tablets without food if needed

facts.content: Follow-up after in-person exam and call support to book appointment.
facts.source_text: Follow-up after in-person exam; call support to book appointment
